The paper uses the isogeometric boundary element method to solve Helmholtz equations for electromagnetic scattering problems.
Non-uniform rational B-splines (NURBS) are employed to construct the structural geometries and discretize the electric and magnetic field integral equations.
The series expansion method is used to decouple the frequency-dependent terms from the integrand in the boundary element method, avoiding time-consuming multi-frequency calculations.
The second-order Arnoldi (SOAR) method is applied to construct a reduced-order model that retains the essential structures and key properties of the original model for large-scale problems.
The proposed approach is demonstrated to be effective and accurate through several numerical examples.
The paper presents a novel fast calculation method for broadband electromagnetic scattering analysis.
The frequency-decoupling technique based on the series expansion method is used to avoid time-consuming multi-frequency calculations.
The model order reduction using the second-order Arnoldi (SOAR) method enables efficient analysis of large-scale electromagnetic scattering problems.
The combination of frequency-decoupling and model order reduction techniques contributes to the efficiency of the proposed approach.
The isogeometric boundary element method provides a more accurate and efficient approach compared to traditional methods for electromagnetic scattering analysis.
The paper aims to address the challenges of time-consuming multi-frequency calculations and large-scale problems in broadband electromagnetic scattering analysis.
The numerical examples presented in the paper demonstrate the correctness and effectiveness of the proposed algorithms.
